Reference for the embedded client introduced in [Your first embedded device](/docs/build/tutorials/embedded-first-device).

## Declaring actions

An action is a `FunctionDefinition` built with `FunctionBuilder`, and a callback that implements it.

```cpp
FunctionBuilder(name, description, argsSize = 1024, returnsSize = 512)
```

`argsSize` and `returnsSize` are the JSON buffer sizes for the definition's ports. Increase them
for actions with many ports.

| Builder method | Adds |
|---|---|
| `argInt`, `argFloat`, `argString`, `argBool` `(key, label, desc, nullable)` | an input port |
| `argStringChoice(key, label, desc, {{"Label", "value"}, ...})` | a string input with a dropdown |
| `argStructure(key, identifier, label, desc, nullable)` | a [structure](/docs/design/terminology/structure) input, passed as its id string |
| `returnInt`, `returnFloat`, `returnString`, `returnBool`, `returnStructure` | an output port |
| `withDefault(key, value)` | a default value for input `key` |
| `withSlider(key, min, max, step)` | a slider widget for number input `key` |

The callback receives the arguments as an ArduinoJson object and answers through a `ReplyChannel`:

```cpp
typedef std::function<bool(ArkitektApp &, Agent &, JsonObject, ReplyChannel &)> AgentFunction;
```

```cpp
auto def = FunctionBuilder("divide", "Divides two numbers")
    .argFloat("a", "A").argFloat("b", "B")
    .returnFloat("result", "Result")
    .build();

app.registerFunction("divide", def,
    [](ArkitektApp &app, Agent &agent, JsonObject args, ReplyChannel &reply) -> bool
    {
        float a = args["a"] | 0.0f;
        float b = args["b"] | 0.0f;
        if (b == 0) { reply.critical("Division by zero"); return true; }

        reply.progress(0.5);
        reply.log("dividing");

        StaticJsonDocument<64> doc;
        JsonObject ret = doc.to<JsonObject>();
        ret["result"] = a / b;
        reply.done(ret);
        return true;
    });
```

| `ReplyChannel` | Sends |
|---|---|
| `done(returns)` / `done()` | the result; the task completes |
| `log(message, level = "INFO")` | a log line on the task |
| `progress(fraction)` | progress, as a value from `0.0` to `1.0` |
| `critical(error)` | an error; the task fails |
| `yield(values)` | an intermediate result (see limits: actions cannot yet be declared as generators) |

Returning `false` from the callback is reported as a failed task.

## State

A device can publish [state](/docs/build/guides/python/state-lifecycle) that Orkestrator shows live
and workflows can [guard](/docs/build/guides/python/durable-execution#guard) on. Declare it with
`StateBuilder` and update single fields with `setPort`. Each update is sent as a patch.

```cpp
app.registerState("sensor_status",
    StateBuilder("sensor_status", "Temperature probe")
        .portFloat("temperature")
        .portInt("readings_count")
        .build());

app.registerBackgroundTask([](ArkitektApp &app, Agent &agent) {
    AgentState *st = agent.getState("sensor_status");
    if (st) st->setPort("temperature", readProbe());
}, 5000);   // every 5 s
```

State fields are `int`, `float`, `String` or `bool`. `registerBackgroundTask(fn, intervalMs)` runs
`fn` from `app.loop()` at the given interval.

## Provisioning and connection

`app.run(cfg)` takes a `RunConfig`:

```cpp
struct RunConfig
{
    bool ble = true;                                 // provision over Bluetooth
    bool enableWpa2Enterprise = true;
    unsigned long bootReconfigureTimeout = 5000;     // hold BOOT this long to reset
    const char *bleDeviceName = "ARKITEKT_CONFIG";
    String redeemToken = "";
    String baseUrl = "";
    uint8_t maxWifiRetries = 3;
};
```

**Over Bluetooth (default).** Pokket writes the WiFi credentials (including enterprise identity
and a CA certificate for eduroam), the server URL and a connection token to the device. These are
stored in the ESP32's non-volatile storage (namespace `arkitekt`) and survive reboots.

**Without Bluetooth.** Set `cfg.ble = false`, `cfg.baseUrl` and `cfg.redeemToken` in the firmware.
The WiFi credentials must already be stored on the device.

On every boot the device:

1. connects to WiFi (`maxWifiRetries` attempts, 20 s each);
2. claims its configuration from the server's fakts endpoint with the stored token, and gets an
   OAuth2 client and the addresses of the services
   ([Service discovery](/docs/build/concepts/service-discovery));
3. gets an access token with the OAuth2 **client-credentials** grant. There is no browser on the
   device, so the token from provisioning is the authorization;
4. picks the first reachable address of each service, registers its actions and states with
   [Rekuest](/docs/build/concepts/services/rekuest) (only when they changed), and opens the agent WebSocket.

If WiFi never worked, or the server rejects the token, the device clears its configuration and
returns to Bluetooth provisioning. To **reset** a device by hand, hold the BOOT button for
`bootReconfigureTimeout` milliseconds while it runs. The WebSocket reconnects every 5 s after a
drop and starts a fresh state session on each reconnect.

## What is not there yet [#what-is-not-there-yet]

| Python client | ESP32 today |
|---|---|
| Cancellation, pause, interrupt | **Not supported.** A running action cannot be stopped from the platform. |
| Concurrent tasks | Actions run one at a time, **synchronously inside `app.loop()`**. A long action also blocks heartbeats and background tasks, so keep actions short. |
| Generators / streaming | `reply.yield()` exists, but an action cannot be declared as a generator |
| Workflows, calling other actions | Not supported |
| [Durable execution](/docs/build/concepts/durable-execution) | No journal. A device that reboots mid-task leaves the task LOST. |
| Types | `int`, `float`, `string`, `bool`, string choices, and structure ids. No lists, dicts, nested models or images. |
| TLS | Connections use TLS when the server does, but **certificates are not verified** |
| Token refresh | None. The access token is fetched at boot, so a device that outlives its token must reboot. |
| Registration | Re-registration is triggered by the number of ports, not their types. Changing a port's type without changing the count needs a version bump. |

Size limits come from fixed JSON buffers: 1 KB for an incoming task's arguments and for a result,
and 8 KB for all action definitions together.

<Callout type="warn" title="Serial output">

The firmware logs verbosely to the serial console, including connection secrets. Do not leave
provisioned devices attached to shared computers with a serial monitor open.

</Callout>
